overview: The two broad stages of any industrial biotechnology production, split by whether the product is still being grown or is already being purified.
genZNote: Upstream: growing the organism and getting it to make the product. Downstream: extracting, purifying, and packaging that product afterward.

aspects.label: Stage of Production
aspects.valueA: Involves selecting the organism, media preparation, and fermentation/culturing to produce the desired biomolecule.
aspects.valueB: Involves separation, purification, and formulation of the product after it has been produced.

aspects.label: Main Activities
aspects.valueA: Strain selection, media optimisation, bioreactor/fermenter operation.
aspects.valueB: Filtration, centrifugation, chromatography, and formulation into a final, marketable product.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Growing genetically engineered bacteria in a bioreactor to produce insulin.
aspects.valueB: Purifying and formulating that insulin into an injectable product.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Both stages together make up 'bioprocess technology' — a frequently tested biotechnology-industry concept, especially for products like insulin and vaccines.
overlay.memoryTrick: Upstream = growing/making it. Downstream = cleaning/packaging it.
overlay.commonMisconception: Downstream processing is not a minor afterthought — it often accounts for the majority of the total cost and complexity of producing a biotech product.
